introduction: Unlike the Himalayan rivers, Peninsular rivers are much 'older' (mature) and are primarily 'seasonal' because they depend almost entirely on monsoon rainfall. Due to the general gradient (slope) of the Peninsular Plateau from west to east, most of these rivers flow eastwards, though a few major ones flow west.

core_concepts.title: East-Flowing Rivers
core_concepts.description: Major rivers include Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Cauvery. These flow eastwards, drain into the Bay of Bengal, and form massive, fertile 'Deltas' at their mouths.

core_concepts.title: West-Flowing Rivers
core_concepts.description: Narmada and Tapi (Tapti) are the most prominent. They flow westwards into the Arabian Sea. Because of the terrain, they do not form deltas; instead, they form 'Estuaries'.

core_concepts.title: The Godavari
core_concepts.description: It is the longest (1465 km) and largest river system of Peninsular India. Due to its massive size and extent, it is also known as the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South) or 'Vridha Ganga' (Old Ganga).

core_concepts.title: The Narmada
core_concepts.description: It is the longest west-flowing river of the Peninsula. It famously flows through a 'Rift Valley' situated between the Vindhya Range in the north and the Satpura Range in the south.

important_entities.name: Dhuandhar Falls
important_entities.significance: The Narmada river creates this spectacular and famous waterfall over the Marble Rocks near Bhedaghat in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Dakshin Ganga vs. Ganga of the South
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common exam trap: 'Godavari' is called the Dakshin Ganga (because of its length and size). However, the 'Cauvery' river is often referred to as the 'Ganga of the South' due to its extreme purity and religious utility.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Sabarmati (Sa), Mahi (Ma), Narmada (N), Tapi (Ta). All of these flow west and drain into the Arabian Sea (Gulf of Khambhat).

exam_strategy_tips: The fact that Narmada and Tapi flow through 'Rift Valleys' and form 'Estuaries' (NOT deltas) is asked in almost every competitive exam.
Always remember that Peninsular rivers are older than Himalayan rivers and have broad, shallow valleys.
